message.content: The sea usually looks blue—especially when it’s clear and calm—but its color can shift depending on depth, weather, time of day, and what’s in the water. In shallow, sandy areas it may appear turquoise or greenish, while in deeper waters it can look a deep navy or even black. Light scattering, algae, and reflections from the sky all play a role in giving the sea its ever‑changing hue.
